subsystems.name: Host material
subsystems.role: the physical system that can host non-abelian quasiparticles.
parts: semiconductor quantum wells (gallium arsenide or indium arsenide)
semiconductor–superconductor hybrids (indium arsenide nanowires with an aluminium shell)
fractional quantum Hall states in a two-dimensional electron gas

subsystems.name: Nanoscale device
subsystems.role: geometry that lets quasiparticles be created, moved and brought together.
parts: epitaxial nanowire networks or planar hybrid islands

subsystems.name: Gate control
subsystems.role: electrostatic gates tune the local potential so quasiparticle modes appear and shift position.

subsystems.name: Readout
subsystems.role: detects the parity (whether a mode pair is occupied) without destroying the state.

subsystems.name: Cryogenic environment
subsystems.role: keeps the device cold enough and shielded from interference.

subsystems.name: Classical control stack
subsystems.role: compiles algorithms into braiding or measurement sequences and interprets the results.

buildSteps.title: Grow the material
buildSteps.detail: Crystalline layers are built atom by atom with molecular beam epitaxy — either quantum-well heterostructures or semiconductor nanowires with a thin superconducting shell grown without breaking vacuum.

buildSteps.title: Pattern the device
buildSteps.detail: Electron-beam lithography and shadow evaporation define superconducting islands, tunnel barriers and contacts with nanometre precision.

buildSteps.title: Add gates and wiring
buildSteps.detail: Dielectric layers and metal gate electrodes are deposited so each segment of the device can be tuned individually.

buildSteps.title: Cool and apply magnetic field
buildSteps.detail: The chip is mounted in a dilution refrigerator at tens of millikelvin, with a magnetic field along the wire and heavy filtering on every line.

buildSteps.title: Look for the signature
buildSteps.detail: Tunnelling spectroscopy searches for a conductance peak pinned at zero bias — the standard, and famously ambiguous, hint of a protected mode.

buildSteps.title: Prove the particles are non-abelian
buildSteps.detail: The decisive test is interferometry or braiding: swapping two quasiparticles must change the state in a way ordinary particles cannot. This has not been achieved in a solid-state device.

buildSteps.title: Form one qubit
buildSteps.detail: Two or more protected modes are combined so their joint parity stores a qubit, and the parity lifetime is measured.

buildSteps.title: Scale into an array
buildSteps.detail: Many such devices are wired into a network, with gates implemented by measurements rather than by physically dragging particles around.

buildSteps.title: Add error correction
buildSteps.detail: A surface-code-style layer of many physical qubits builds logical qubits and tolerates the residual errors.

prerequisites.tech: Non-abelian anyons in a controllable device
prerequisites.why: without them there is no topological qubit — only candidate signatures that are hard to distinguish from disorder.
defects and unwanted subgap states mimic the signal being sought and can destroy protection.
dilution refrigerators and filtered wiring are standard, though wiring thousands of gates into one fridge is unsolved.
epitaxy and lithography are good enough to build single devices but not yet uniform arrays.
codes exist and are being demonstrated on other qubit types; applying them to topological hardware is untested.

pathway.milestone: single nanowire and quantum-well devices showing candidate signatures, with a 2025 interferometric parity measurement reported and still debated by the community
pathway.unlocks: a narrowing of which material systems are worth pursuing.

pathway.milestone: an unambiguous demonstration of non-abelian exchange in a solid-state device
pathway.unlocks: confidence that the underlying physics is real and not noise.

pathway.milestone: one topological qubit whose stored parity clearly outlives the equivalent in conventional qubits
pathway.unlocks: the claimed hardware advantage of the approach.

pathway.milestone: small arrays with a working error-correction decoder
pathway.unlocks: scaling from tens of qubits to hundreds.

pathway.milestone: fault-tolerant machines running cryptographic and materials-simulation workloads
pathway.unlocks: the same applications as other quantum computers, but with far lower error-correction overhead if the protection holds.
